answer: Meadow Ration Registry: each identity must hold a unique, non-transferable plot allocation issued by a regional land registry, capped one per verified physical parcel. Registries cross-check plot boundaries, so claiming two identities requires acquiring two disjoint parcels with clean title. A gale of audit requests can challenge any allocation; failure forfeits it permanently. Attacker cost: legal acquisition and maintenance of separate titled land, plus forfeiture risk — a scarce geographic resource, not capital, that cannot be rented or jade-brokered at scale without detection.
